status: Design only; no generated code or shapes may execute under this contract alone
scope: Future controlled generation and execution evaluation; existing authored row-graph baseline is separate

tracks.direct_decision: LLM emits decisions per fixed batch without tool execution; shared parsing metadata means this is not raw-only LLM
tracks.ad_hoc_code: One batch-specific Python artifact per fixed batch, discarded for reuse but retained as evidence
tracks.reusable_python: One Python artifact built on common development materials, frozen and reused across evaluation batches
tracks.reusable_shacl: One SHACL artifact built on the same development materials, frozen and reused across evaluation batches

fairness.construction_input: Same policy text, definitions, mapping specification, parsing semantics and predeclared development examples for both reusable arms; no evaluation rows or labels during construction
fairness.execution_input: Same raw rows and normalized metadata for every automated arm; SHACL runtime additionally materializes the equivalent mapped graph without adding facts
fairness.ad_hoc_exposure: Ad hoc code sees the current evaluation batch by definition; report this architectural difference, not equal construction exposure
fairness.retry_policy: No automatic retry, repair or reference-based correction. Any later diagnostic is separately authorized, reviewed and reported with original attempt retained
fairness.review_boundary: Operational review checks the harness and isolation, not correctness of model artifacts. Human semantic corrections create a separate assisted condition
fairness.cost_reporting: Report per-batch generation versus amortized reusable construction separately, plus total cost over the complete common cohort; manual effort remains unmeasured unless prospectively logged

artifact_envelope.python: UTF-8 source defining evaluate(packet), returning the existing decisions schema; retain exact original source
artifact_envelope.shacl: UTF-8 Turtle with three named policy root shapes; runner attaches targets from the public policy eligibility rules, not reference labels. Each root is executed separately
artifact_envelope.target_policy: Model-authored target declarations are unsupported in primary SHACL scope; they are rejected as unsupported artifact, never silently removed
artifact_envelope.unknown_handling: Shared eligibility metadata and explicit public policy contract are available to all arms. SHACL adapter emits unknown before validation where required. Python/direct outputs are not silently repaired if they mishandle unknown
artifact_envelope.limitation: Unknown prechecks enforce part of the declared policy in the SHACL harness; measure that intervention separately rather than attribute all correctness to generated shapes
artifact_envelope.python_intake: Syntax-only byte-preserving intake, maximum65536bytes, strictUTF8. No code-fence stripping or repair; accepted syntax is not execution approval or interface/semantic validation.

evaluation.denominator: All predeclared row-policy keys remain in the original denominator, including failures and missing outputs
evaluation.semantic_policy: A syntactically supported but wrong artifact must execute and be scored as wrong; intake must not compare to expected answers
evaluation.primary: End-to-end results including all failures, abstention and coverage
evaluation.secondary: Conditional valid-artifact execution results reported with explicit selected denominator; never replace primary results
evaluation.failure_expansion: A reusable artifact construction failure affects every planned evaluation key for that arm; batch-specific failure affects only its declared batch
evaluation.reference_access: Scorer-only labels and reference implementation excluded from execution inputs and mounted files
evaluation.ad_hoc_endpoint: Primary score uses executable decisions returned by generated Python, with no subsequent model finalization call. Any later model-written explanation is a separate diagnostic and cannot replace primary decisions.

execution_requirements.python: A separately reviewed OS-enforced execution boundary, not eval/exec or a subprocess timeout described as a sandbox. No network, credentials or host workspace access; readonly input, temporary output, fixed dependencies, resource and output limits
execution_requirements.shacl: Equivalent resource and network restrictions. No remote imports, SHACL-JS, external services or unrestricted extensions. Supported SHACL Core/SPARQL subset must be enumerated before launch; parser allowlisting alone is not an isolation boundary
execution_requirements.limits: Wall time, memory, output bytes, artifact bytes and dependency versions must be concrete and frozen before execution
execution_requirements.failure_trace: Retain raw artifact, parse/support decision, exit or timeout, stderr, actual validation report when available; distinguish attempted execution from completed validation

launch_gates: Separately reviewed implemented isolation and adversarial development checks
